fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeAdjoin: A building on the limit is exempt from R.111-17 on that edge; the envelope does not draw that case.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeAlignm: Where no opposite alignment was found for a street edge, R.111-16’s slope rises from that edge itself: stricter than the rule.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeApprox: The envelope’s outline is the Site boundary set back, edge by edge, by the largest confirmed setback of the edge’s role (street, side or rear); a street setback is measured from the street edge’s line, which runs on past the plot’s corners.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeBounda: A height that depends on the distance to the Site boundary is measured from the ground at the boundary’s nearest point, the boundary standing for the limit.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeChecks: The checks, not the volume, say whether the design is within the rules.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeFacade: The rule limits the façade height; the volume draws it as a ceiling over the whole building, which is stricter than the rule for a roof rising behind the façade.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeHeight: In the volume, a height is measured from the ground at each point (the terrain drawn), not from a façade’s foot.
In the volume, a height drawn on the plan applies only inside the prescription’s outline (where the outline and the prescription overlap).
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeLattic: The 3D volume is computed about every metre: exact at each computed point; between two points, near the ends or re-entrant corners of a limit whose height depends on the distance, it may stand above the rule by at most half the slope per metre.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeNotApp: The envelope draws only the rules listed as applied in its view; a confirmed rule it cannot draw (a façade height, a maximum setback, a ratio, a distance between buildings) still limits the design.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeReentr: At a re-entrant corner of the Site boundary, and where a side or rear limit ends at an open corner, the outline follows the rounded line at the setback, drawn as straight pieces just inside it: stricter than the rule.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.envelopeSetbac: The required setback line drawn on the plan replaces the opposite alignment.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.existingAsMode: Existing building as modelled; the regulation means it as it stood when the plan was approved ({date}).
fr-urban-rules.assumption.existingReplac: The existing building is to be replaced: it is not counted.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.facadeHeightFo: The façade height is measured from the wall’s foot to its top, sample by sample; a lexicon that measures it otherwise is to be read.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.featuresCapped: Only {count} features are drawn: the derived bands past them are left out.
fr-urban-rules.assumption.floorToFloorDe: Floor-to-floor taken as {height} m, the editor’s default storey height: the storeys’ own height is not available to this extension.

fr-urban-rules.assumption.overhangsUnsup: Roof overhangs are taken as not supported by posts (the model has no posts), so not counted; add one on posts as a balcony area.
